test_name: PIK3CA variant resolution to specific codon (therascreen PIK3CA RGQ PCR Kit hotspots or FoundationOne CDx) covering C420R, E542K, E545A/D/G/K, Q546E/R, H1047L/R/Y
tissue_type: archival FFPE (breast primary or liver M1) or plasma ctDNA
rationale: The profile says PIK3CA is mutated but does not specify the codon, and the FDA companion diagnostics for alpelisib (therascreen PIK3CA) and the F1CDx label for capivasertib (PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN) only call a tumor 'PIK3CA-altered' for the 11-variant hotspot set: C420R, E542K, E545A/D/G/K, Q546E/R, H1047L/R/Y. A non-hotspot helical or kinase-domain variant does not get a patient onto an alpelisib-labeled regimen and may or may not be accepted by capivasertib protocols, so the resolution gates which PI3K/AKT-axis drug can be offered at all. If the existing NGS already names the codon, this row collapses to a documentation check; if it does not, a hotspot-aware confirmation is the rate-limiting step before any PI3K-axis discussion (pmid:31091374, pmid:35613031).
turnaround_estimate: 2-4 weeks (tissue NGS); 7-10 days (therascreen PCR if used as a confirmatory)
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable
decision_gated: Alpelisib, inavolisib, and capivasertib eligibility; trial enrollment for PI3K/AKT-axis studies that require a hotspot-defined PIK3CA call.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FDA-approved companion diagnostic for capivasertib in HR+/HER2- breast cancer; the most defensible single tissue assay because it resolves PIK3CA hotspot, AKT1 E17K, PTEN status, and TMB on one report and bundles with the orthogonal NGS row downstream.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: Original FDA companion diagnostic for alpelisib; runs the 11-variant hotspot set on tissue and ctDNA. Useful when speed beats breadth and the only question is alpelisib eligibility.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: FDA-approved 648-gene panel; equivalent breadth to FoundationOne CDx.

providers.name: Guardant Health
providers.notes: Plasma alternative when tumor tissue is unavailable; PIK3CA hotspots are reliably detected at clinically meaningful VAF.

notes: If the existing tumor NGS report names a specific PIK3CA codon, treat this row as a chart-review confirmation rather than a new send-out. If only 'PIK3CA mutated' is recorded, push for the hotspot resolution before any PI3K-axis therapy is discussed.

test_name: PTEN IHC (clone 138G6 or SP218) with positive internal control, scored as deficient if <10% tumor-cell staining at any intensity
tissue_type: archival FFPE (breast primary or liver M1)
rationale: Copy-number loss on NGS does not always translate to PTEN protein loss; PTEN is frequently inactivated by promoter methylation, frameshift, or LOH not picked up by panels with limited copy-number resolution. The FDA approval of capivasertib (CAPItello-291) and the F1CDx companion-diagnostic label define 'PTEN-altered' on a DNA call, but the IHC re-stain with a <10% cutoff (validated in the 2025 Virchows Archiv series) is the orthogonal protein-level confirmation that pathologists and tumor boards expect before AKT-inhibitor discussion. Skipping it leaves the AKT-inhibitor rationale resting on a single copy-number signal without protein-level corroboration (pmid:40931235, pmid:39101942).
turnaround_estimate: 5-7 business days once block is pulled
decision_gated: Capivasertib + fulvestrant (HR+/HER2-) decision; trial enrollment for AKT-inhibitor protocols in TNBC where PTEN-deficient status is required by IHC.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Validated PTEN IHC protocol with the 138G6 clone and a documented internal-control standard; the most defensible reference for the <10% deficiency call.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: CAP-accredited commercial option with shorter turnaround than the academic centers.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service

notes: Read alongside the comprehensive tumor NGS so the molecular (copy-number) and protein-level (IHC) calls can be integrated by the same pathologist.

test_name: TMB measurement on an FDA-cleared comprehensive genomic panel sized ≥0.8 Mb (FoundationOne CDx, MSK-IMPACT, or Tempus xT CDx), with the panel and threshold documented in the report
rationale: The tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab approval (KEYNOTE-158) is anchored on FoundationOne CDx as the companion diagnostic at a ≥10 mut/Mb cutoff, and TMB values are not interchangeable across panels: smaller or differently-bioinformatic panels can over- or under-call TMB by 3-5 mut/Mb at the clinically-relevant threshold. A 14 mut/Mb value from a non-FDA-cleared assay near the 10 mut/Mb cutoff is exactly the situation where the call should be locked to a panel the FDA label recognizes before pembrolizumab is offered on a TMB-only basis. Confirmation also lets the tumor board document which panel made the call for prior authorization (pmid:32919526, guideline:fda-label-pembrolizumab-tmb-2020).
turnaround_estimate: 2-4 weeks if a new comprehensive panel is needed; same-day chart review if the existing report already names the panel
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable
decision_gated: Tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab eligibility under KEYNOTE-158; TMB-restricted trial enrollment.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: The only FDA-approved companion diagnostic for TMB at the ≥10 mut/Mb threshold used in the KEYNOTE-158 tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab label. If the existing TMB call came from another assay, this is the defensible re-run.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: FDA-approved 648-gene panel; TMB methodology has been benchmarked against FoundationOne CDx but is not the panel named in the pembrolizumab label.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Academic-center alternative; the panel size (~1.5 Mb) is well-validated for TMB but the assay is generally not available outside the MSK network.

notes: If the original 14 mut/Mb call came from FoundationOne CDx this row collapses to a chart-review documentation check; if it came from any other assay, re-run on F1CDx before using the value to gate pembrolizumab.

test_name: PD-L1 IHC (22C3 pharmDx CPS for pembrolizumab; SP142 IC for atezolizumab if relevant)
tissue_type: archival FFPE (breast primary preferred over liver M1)
rationale: In metastatic TNBC the pembrolizumab + chemotherapy label (KEYNOTE-355) requires PD-L1 CPS ≥10 by the 22C3 pharmDx companion diagnostic; in early-stage TNBC the KEYNOTE-522 indication is PD-L1-agnostic. The case is de novo M1, so PD-L1 CPS is the rate-limiting biomarker for the 1L ICI + chemo decision, and PD-L1 expression in TNBC is discordant between primary breast and liver metastasis in roughly 20-30% of paired samples (pmid:34626408, pmid:31166680). Skipping it means defaulting to PD-L1-agnostic backbones and missing the chance to anchor a CPS ≥10 case onto the pembrolizumab + chemo regimen.
decision_gated: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-355) in 1L metastatic TNBC; CPS ≥10 anchors the indication.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: FDA-approved companion diagnostic for pembrolizumab in metastatic TNBC; widely available with national next-day turnaround. The most defensible single assay for the KEYNOTE-355 CPS ≥10 cutoff.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: CAP-accredited; fastest commercial turnaround in our experience.

notes: Order on the breast primary block; if only liver M1 is available, run on both and note the discordance rate in the report.

test_name: Germline BRCA1/2 sequencing plus del/dup, ideally on a hereditary breast/ovarian cancer panel that also covers PALB2, ATM, CHEK2, BARD1, RAD51C/D, BRIP1, TP53, PTEN, CDH1, STK11
rationale: The tumor NGS call does not say whether the BRCA1 variant is germline or somatic, and the answer changes a 42-year-old patient's life: germline BRCA1 carriers face bilateral mastectomy and risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy decisions and trigger cascade testing of first-degree relatives, while a purely somatic BRCA1 still supports PARP-inhibitor and platinum sensitivity but does not drive surgical or family-screening choices. NCCN BINV/genetic-familial breast guidelines mandate germline testing in any patient diagnosed under 50 or with TNBC regardless of age. Skipping this means missing a near-certain risk-management conversation and leaving family members untested.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) or saliva kit
decision_gated: Risk-reducing surgery decisions (bilateral mastectomy, RRSO), cascade testing of first-degree relatives, and confirmatory eligibility for germline-BRCA-restricted trials.

providers.name: Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae)
providers.assay_brand: Invitae Hereditary Breast and Gyn Cancers Panel (Multi-Cancer Panel option)
providers.notes: Highest-volume hereditary breast/ovarian panel in the US; broad payer acceptance and a financial-assistance program that meaningfully reduces patient out-of-pocket. Pairs cleanly with downstream cascade-testing logistics for first-degree relatives.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: Original BRCA reference lab; useful when the treating center has a long-standing Myriad relationship.

providers.name: Ambry Genetics
providers.notes: Caris-owned. Equivalent multi-cancer hereditary panel.

notes: Pair the germline report with a cancer-genetics counseling visit before the result returns so cascade testing of the patient's siblings and first-degree relatives can be triggered the same week the variant is classified.

test_name: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) genomic-scar score (Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS, or equivalent on FoundationOne CDx / Caris MI Profile)
rationale: An HRD score (LOH + telomeric allelic imbalance + large-scale state transitions) gives orthogonal proof that the BRCA1 variant is producing a functional HR-deficient phenotype, not just sitting at a permissive VAF. This matters most when the BRCA1 call sits in a domain whose functional consequence is debatable, or when later resistance lines need a baseline scar score to interpret BRCA reversion in ctDNA. The score does not gate PARP-inhibitor eligibility in BRCA1-mutated TNBC (that runs off the BRCA call itself), but it strengthens the platinum/PARPi rationale and frames any future HR-targeted trial discussion (pmid:33037126, pmid:32826325).
decision_gated: Strength of HR-deficient phenotype call; complements the PARP-inhibitor and platinum rationale rather than gating it.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.assay_brand: MyChoice CDx (HRD with Genomic Instability Score)
providers.notes: The only FDA-approved HRD companion diagnostic in the US; the most widely-recognized HRD assay in the literature and in trial protocols. Pivotal-trial validated for niraparib in ovarian cancer; widely used off-label as the HRD reference in breast cancer.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Reports a genome-wide LOH score; not the same algorithm as MyChoice CDx but a reasonable orthogonal call when MyChoice is unavailable.

notes: Most informative when the BRCA1 variant is a VUS or sits in a domain where functional consequence is debatable; less critical if the BRCA1 call is a clear loss-of-function variant.

test_name: PAM50 intrinsic-subtype assay (NanoString Prosigna or Agendia BluePrint) with concurrent Lehmann TNBCtype-4 (BL1/BL2/M/LAR) classification on RNA-seq data
rationale: Roughly 25% of TNBCs do not classify as PAM50 basal-like, and within basal-like the Lehmann TNBCtype-4 subdivision (BL1, BL2, M, LAR) carries divergent neoadjuvant pCR rates: BL1 ~52% versus BL2 ~0%, LAR ~10%, M ~23% under anthracycline-taxane backbones (pmid:29521352, pmid:21633166, pmid:31836816). The current 'basal-like' call should be locked to the assay that made it (PAM50 vs ad-hoc gene set), and the Lehmann layer adds therapeutic resolution that the basal/non-basal binary cannot: LAR enrichment shifts the conversation toward AR-directed agents, M/MSL shifts it away from KEYNOTE-style ICI + taxane, and BL1 reinforces the platinum/PARP backbone already supported by BRCA1.
decision_gated: TNBC-subtype-directed therapy bias (AR-axis vs platinum/PARP vs ICI + taxane); trial-enrollment refinement for subtype-restricted protocols.

providers.name: Veracyte (Prosigna / NanoString assets)
providers.address: 6000 Shoreline Court, Suite 300, South San Francisco, CA 94080
providers.notes: FDA-cleared PAM50 intrinsic-subtype call; the most defensible US assay for the basal-like-vs-non-basal question. Veracyte acquired the NanoString diagnostics business in 2024.

providers.name: Agendia
providers.notes: Reports basal-type vs luminal-type vs HER2-type signatures; a reasonable orthogonal call when Prosigna is unavailable.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome RNA-seq; supports Lehmann TNBCtype-4 classification when run through the published TNBCtype-4 caller.

notes: If the current basal-like call already came from Prosigna or BluePrint, the priority drops to medium and the action collapses to confirming subtype on the existing report.

test_name: Baseline ctDNA for BRCA1 reversion / secondary mutation surveillance (Guardant360, FoundationOne Liquid CDx, or Natera Signatera tumor-informed assay)
tissue_type: 5-10 mL plasma (Streck tube); Signatera also needs an FFPE block for assay design
rationale: BRCA1/2 reversion mutations are detectable in ctDNA in roughly 60% of patients who progress on PARP inhibitors and are the single most common acquired-resistance mechanism in BRCA-mutated breast cancer (pmid:38302062). A baseline draw before any PARP-inhibitor or platinum exposure gives a clean reference for downstream resistance interpretation; serial draws after first progression let the team distinguish on-pathway resistance (reversion) from off-pathway escape (PI3K-axis activation, secondary RAD51 lesions). Without a baseline the reversion call becomes ambiguous when she later progresses on olaparib or talazoparib.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks for tumor-naive panels; 4-6 weeks for Signatera baseline build
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL plasma (Streck tube). Signatera baseline also needs an FFPE block.
decision_gated: Acquired PARP-inhibitor and platinum resistance surveillance; informs whether to push through resistance or switch to a non-HR-axis therapy.

providers.name: Guardant Health
providers.notes: Tumor-naive plasma panel with broad BRCA1/2 coverage; fastest turnaround for the baseline draw and the panel most commonly cited in the reversion-mutation literature. Best fit when the goal is fast resistance-mechanism interpretation at progression rather than deep low-VAF MRD.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Equivalent tumor-naive plasma panel; preferred if the FoundationOne CDx tissue assay is already the comprehensive-panel choice so the same vendor reads tissue and plasma.

providers.name: Natera
providers.address: 13011 McCallen Pass, Building A, Austin, TX 78753
providers.notes: Tumor-informed; the deepest MRD sensitivity but the bespoke-panel design needs a tumor block and a 4-6 week build window. Best added once the systemic plan is set.

notes: Schedule the baseline draw before any PARP-inhibitor or platinum exposure so post-treatment reversions can be unambiguously called as acquired.

test_name: International TILs Working Group (ITWG) stromal-TIL re-scoring on H&E by a dedicated breast pathologist (Salgado 2014 methodology; 0-100% scale on a single tumor-bearing section)
rationale: The '3+ stromal TILs (high)' label sits cleanly with the ITWG methodology only if it was scored as a continuous 0-100% percentage on a single H&E section by a pathologist trained on the Salgado 2014 guideline; ad-hoc '1+/2+/3+' grading is a known pitfall and inflates inter-observer variability (pmid:32195312, pmid:25214542). The re-score does not gate ICI eligibility (TIL-rich status is informative, not labeled), but it is the reference standard the ImPACT/KEYNOTE-522 literature uses and it makes the TIL signal defensible at tumor board. If the original call was already done by a breast pathologist using the percentage scale, this row collapses to a documentation check.
decision_gated: ICI-combination rationale strength (KEYNOTE-522, IMpassion-style); reinforces but does not gate enrollment.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service
providers.notes: MSK breast pathology is among the highest-volume breast-TIL scoring groups in the US and routinely contributes to ITWG TIL working-group studies; the most defensible expert second-read.

providers.name: Dana-Farber / Brigham and Women's Pathology
providers.notes: Stuart Schnitt's breast-pathology group; established TIL scoring expertise.

notes: If the original TIL call came from a non-breast pathologist or used '1+/2+/3+' notation rather than the percentage scale, the re-score moves to priority high.

test_name: MYC FISH (8q24 break-apart / amplification probe set) or MYC IHC (clone Y69) on archival FFPE
rationale: MYC amplification by NGS copy-number is a reasonably specific call but the magnitude (low-level gain vs focal high-level amplification) varies by panel and tumor purity. FISH or IHC arbitrates this for the BET/CDK7/CDK9 trial rationale, which generally favors high-level amplification or strong protein overexpression rather than borderline gain (pmid:32913096, pmid:34607981). The result refines trial eligibility for MYC-pathway protocols but does not gate any approved therapy.
decision_gated: Refines MYC-amplification call strength for BET/CDK7/CDK9 trial enrollment; does not gate approved therapy.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: High-volume commercial FISH lab; standard 8q24 amplification probe set with same-week turnaround.

notes: If a comprehensive panel (FoundationOne CDx, MSK-IMPACT) has already called MYC amplified with a copy-number value, this row can be deferred unless trial enrollment specifically requires FISH.

test_name: B2M and HLA class I IHC (B2M EP2978Y; HLA-ABC EMR8-5) on archival FFPE, plus B2M / HLA-A/B/C variant call review on the existing tumor NGS panel
rationale: B2M loss and HLA class I antigen-presentation defects are well-characterized primary-resistance mechanisms for ICI in TMB-high and MSI-H tumors; loss of cell-surface MHC class I removes the substrate that PD-1 blockade depends on (pmid:29070816, pmid:38092534). In a TMB-14 / TIL-rich / MSS TNBC the ICI rationale is strong, but a B2M-deficient subclone would predict primary ICI failure even with the favorable TIL and TMB signals, and is detectable on the same FFPE block used for PD-L1 and TIL re-scoring. Optional but cheap to add at the same time as the PD-L1 stain.
tissue_required_estimate: 1-2 unstained slides; can share the PD-L1 / TIL block
decision_gated: Primary-resistance risk for pembrolizumab and other PD-1/PD-L1 agents; refines the ICI rationale without gating it.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.assay_brand: B2M IHC / HLA Class I IHC
providers.notes: Routine commercial IHC; bundle on the same requisition as the PD-L1 22C3 order.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service

notes: Lower priority than PD-L1 CPS or TIL re-scoring; consider only if there is meaningful clinical concern about ICI primary resistance or if the same FFPE block is already going out for several stains.

test_name: Comprehensive NGS review for replication-stress / DDR co-alterations (ATM, ATR, CHK1/2, CDK12, CCNE1 amplification) and TP53 variant-functional classification
tissue_type: archival FFPE; same comprehensive panel as the PIK3CA/PTEN confirmation
rationale: TP53 mutation is near-universal in basal-like TNBC and not directly drug-gating, but it anchors the replication-stress phenotype that WEE1 inhibitors (adavosertib, debio-0123) and ATR inhibitors (ceralasertib, elimusertib) exploit. The actionability hinges on co-alterations: CCNE1 amplification, CDK12 loss, or ATM loss meaningfully shift the WEE1/ATR rationale, and TP53 missense vs nonsense vs hotspot R175H/R248Q/R273H functional class also affects experimental-trial enrollment (pmid:32499663, pmid:31754023). The single comprehensive NGS panel covering this row also covers the PIK3CA hotspot, PTEN status, and TMB rows, so the cost is shared.
turnaround_estimate: 2-4 weeks if new panel; same-day if existing report covers these genes
tissue_required_estimate: shared with the PIK3CA / PTEN / TMB block
decision_gated: WEE1/ATR-inhibitor trial enrollment rationale; not gating for any approved therapy.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Covers TP53, ATM, ATR, CHK1/2, CDK12, and CCNE1 on a single report; the most efficient bundle if FoundationOne CDx is already the chosen comprehensive panel.

notes: If the existing tumor NGS panel already covers these genes, this row collapses to a chart-review pass; no new send-out required.

test_name: IRS2 RNA expression on tumor RNA-seq (Tempus xR, Caris MI Profile WTS, or research RNA-seq) with reference to the TCGA TNBC distribution
rationale: IRS2 copy-number amplification only matters clinically if it translates to elevated IRS2 transcript and a functional IGF-1R/IRS signaling readout; many copy-number gains in TNBC do not. RNA-level confirmation is the cheapest way to triage whether IRS2 is worth chasing on an IGF-1R-axis trial (a small and largely-stalled trial space) versus parking it as a passenger event. Not gating any approved therapy; deferrable until an IGF-1R-axis protocol is on the table.
tissue_required_estimate: FFPE block or 10 unstained slides; can bundle with the PAM50/Lehmann RNA-seq order
decision_gated: IGF-1R/IRS-axis trial enrollment; does not gate approved therapy.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: Reports IRS2 transcript expression alongside the rest of the transcriptome; bundle with the Lehmann subtype call so a single RNA-seq order resolves both.

notes: Defer until an IGF-1R-axis trial is the candidate plan; IRS2 amplification is currently trial-territory only.
